description:
KEYSTONE for every text-processing ticket in fz-5xp.

native_codegen/receive.rs:654 handles Region::Bitstring by calling emit_bitstring_test
(receive.rs:1083) -- a complete implementation with emit_bitstring_like_guard, field
extraction, and variable-size bindings over fz_bs_reader_init_ref / fz_bs_read_field_ref.

jobs/native.rs:3092 returns an error for the SAME region:
  "native entry-dispatch lowering does not support bitstring tests yet"

So native codegen has two dispatch-region lowerings and only one is finished.

PROVEN at 67e09d373 -- the identical pattern, both positions:
  receive do <<len, payload::binary-size(len), rest::binary>> -> len end  => 3  (native OK)
  case m  do <<len, payload::binary-size(len), rest::binary>> -> len end  => native lowering failure

Extraction already works natively outside dispatch: <<a, b, rest::binary>> = s yields
{1, 2, <<3, 4>>} on the native path. Only the boolean region TEST is absent.

DONE = one region-test emitter serves both dispatch sites (fold, do not copy), and
fixtures2/00310_binary_pattern_header.fz + 00311_binary_variable_size.fz pass on run
and build, not just interp. Those two carry no frontmatter and no defer: today, and
the matrix only scans fixtures2/behavior/, so they are currently ungated on native --
move or mirror them into behavior/ so the parity gate actually covers this.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to this ticket's framing, verified before anyone starts it.

I filed this as "one region-test emitter serves both dispatch sites (fold, do not copy)". That is not accurate: the two sites are at DIFFERENT LAYERS.

  native_codegen/receive.rs:1083  emit_bitstring_test emits CRANELIFT IR directly --
                                  a FunctionBuilder, explicit basic blocks,
                                  b.ins().brif(cmp, true_b, &[], false_b, &[]).
                                  ~151 lines.
  jobs/native.rs:3093             entry dispatch emits FZ IR -- ctx.emit_let(Prim::...)
                                  returning a Var, lowered to Cranelift later.

So there is no single function both can call as written.

THE GOOD NEWS is that the primitives are already there and already used in this
very file. jobs/native.rs emits Prim::BitReaderInit, Prim::BitReadField and
Prim::BitReaderDone today -- that is how an irrefutable binding like
`<<a, b, rest :: binary>> = s` extracts natively (verified: it yields
{1, 2, <<3, 4>>} on the native door at HEAD). What is missing is using those
primitives to build a boolean TEST for clause selection, not the ability to read
a bitstring.

So the work is: express Region::Bitstring at the IR layer with the reader prims
already in use here, mirroring the SEMANTICS emit_bitstring_test implements
(the bitstring-like guard, per-field extraction, and variable-size bindings such
as `binary-size(len)`). Read that function as the specification.

Worth deciding while doing it: whether the receive path should then be re-expressed
in terms of the IR-level construction too, so the semantics stop living twice --
that is the actual fold, and it is the reason to prefer mirroring the existing
implementation over inventing a second reading of the shape.

Still verified, unchanged: identical pattern, both positions, at HEAD.
  receive do <<len, payload::binary-size(len), rest::binary>> -> len end  => 3, native OK
  case m  do <<len, payload::binary-size(len), rest::binary>> -> len end  => native lowering failure
And fixtures2/00310_binary_pattern_header.fz / 00311_binary_variable_size.fz carry no
frontmatter and no defer:, and the matrix only scans fixtures2/behavior/, so they are
currently ungated on the native door -- move or mirror them into behavior/ so the
parity gate actually covers this.

INVESTIGATION COMPLETE -- everything below verified against HEAD.

THERE ARE THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS OF THIS TEST, not two. Same shape as fz-5xp.18.
  ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs:591  dispatch_read_bitstring -> bool          WORKS
  native_codegen/receive.rs:1083  emit_bitstring_test (Cranelift)          WORKS
  jobs/native.rs:3093             entry dispatch                           MISSING
That is exactly why `case <<len, rest::binary>> -> ...` runs on interp and fails
to lower natively. Whoever implements the third should decide whether the other
two can then be expressed in terms of it, or this becomes a fourth reading of
the same shape.

TWO HOLES, and they are connected:
  jobs/native.rs:3093  Region::Bitstring                 -- the boolean test
  jobs/native.rs:3287  ProjectionKind::BitstringField(i) -- reading a bound field
The second is largely solved by the first: dispatch_subject_var returns early on
state.values.get(&subject) (:3245), so a test that INSERTS each extracted field
into state.values never reaches the projection error. receive.rs does exactly
this via bitstring_field_subject (receive.rs:1153), which finds the SubjectId
whose source is Projection{source, BitstringField(index)}.

THE IR CAN ALREADY EXPRESS IT. jobs/native.rs emits all of these today, for
irrefutable bindings:
  Prim::BitReaderInit(source)                       -> reader
  Prim::BitReadField{reader, ty, size, endian, signed, unit, is_last} -> result
  Prim::TupleField(result, 0|1|2)                   -> ok | value | next_reader
  Prim::BitReaderDone(reader)                       -> done flag
  lower_bit_size_ir(world, &spec.size, env)         -> size operand
The difference is that the binding path calls ctx.assert_truthy(ok) -- it ABORTS
on a non-match -- where a region test must yield a boolean.

READS CANNOT BE CHAINED UNCONDITIONALLY. On failure fz_bs_read_field allocates a
ONE-tuple [false], not a three-tuple (ir_runtime.rs, "Failure path: alloc
1-tuple [false]"). So TupleField(result, 1) and TupleField(result, 2) after a
failed read are out of bounds. The test needs short-circuit control flow; an AND
over all the ok flags is unsound.

THE CONTROL-FLOW IDIOM IS ALREADY IN THIS FILE. lower_guard_dispatch
(jobs/native.rs:3140) is the template:
    let done_value = ctx.builder.fresh_var();
    let done_b = ctx.builder.block(vec![done_value]);
    let fail_b = ctx.builder.block(vec![]);
    ... ctx.set_term(Term::If{cond, then_b, else_b, origin}) ...
    ctx.current_block = fail_b;
    let (false_value, _) = ctx.emit_let(Prim::Const(Const::False));
    ctx.set_term(Term::Goto(done_b, vec![false_value]));
    ctx.current_block = done_b;
    Ok(done_value)
lower_dispatch_region returns a Var and its caller branches on it (:2922), so a
region is free to build blocks internally as long as it leaves current_block at
a join that defines the result.

SHAPE TYPES: dispatch_matrix/mod.rs:213. BitstringShape{fields, require_done};
BitstringFieldShape{kind, size, endian, signed, unit}; BitstringFieldSize is
Literal(u32) | Binding(SubjectId) | BindingName(String) -- so `binary-size(len)`
resolves through a subject, which is why field extraction must land in
state.values before a later field's size is computed.

ALGORITHM, from emit_bitstring_test: bitstring-like guard -> reader_init -> per
field { compute size, build field spec, read, branch on ok, bind extracted, take
next reader } -> if require_done, check the reader is exhausted -> true.

GATE: fixtures2/00310_binary_pattern_header.fz and 00311_binary_variable_size.fz
have no frontmatter and no defer:, and the matrix only scans fixtures2/behavior/,
so they are ungated on the native door today. Move or mirror them into behavior/
so the parity gate covers this, and add a case/ multi-clause fixture with an
Elixir oracle.

title: Fold the two native bitstring region-test emitters into one
